Formulation
Predisposing: Personal history of hypothyroidism; family history of suicide.  
Precipitating: Recent job change (2 months ago) leading to adjustment stress; possible thyroid dysregulation.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing fatigue, insomnia, decreased appetite reducing activity and mood; possible inadequate thyroid control.  
Protective: Supportive spouse, insight, help-seeking behavior, absence of current suicidal thoughts.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Low mood/fatigue (provisional depressive disorder)
- Patient Goal(s): “Return to previous state,” regain energy, normal appetite and concentration
- Clinical Goal(s): Clarify diagnosis; improve mood/energy; rule out/optimise medical contributors (thyroid, anemia, etc.)
- Actions (Patient):
  • Book and attend in-person GP appointment within next few days  
  • Complete recommended blood tests  
  • Keep brief mood/sleep log until review  
  • Engage in regular light exercise as tolerated; maintain routine sleep schedule
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Arrange physical examination and investigations (thyroid function, CBC, metabolic panel, iron studies)  
  • Screen for depression with validated tool (e.g., PHQ-9) at next visit  
  • Provide psychoeducation on sleep hygiene and mood monitoring  
  • Review thyroid medication dosing and compliance; adjust if needed  
  • Consider referral for psychological therapy (e.g., CBT) depending on investigation results and symptom severity  
  • Schedule follow-up within 2 weeks to review results and reassess mood and risk

Secondary Problem: Insomnia
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve restorative sleep
- Clinical Goal(s): Improve sleep quantity/quality
- Actions (Patient):
  • Implement sleep hygiene measures (consistent bedtime, screen reduction, relaxation techniques)  
  • Limit caffeine/alcohol in evening (if applicable)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide written sleep hygiene resources  
  • Evaluate need for short-term pharmacologic or non-pharmacologic interventions if insomnia persists

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Nature of depressive symptoms, relationship with thyroid disease, plan for investigations, importance of follow-up, sleep hygiene
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Escalating fatigue, persistent low mood, loss of interest, emergence of suicidal thoughts
- Coping Strategies: Structured daily routine, graded exercise, relaxation techniques, communication with spouse/supports, prompt contact with GP if symptoms worsen

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not applicable (telehealth) – to be provided at in-person review
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: Within 2 weeks post-blood-tests, or sooner if risk changes
